core_obligations: Before forming a free union, identify the two possible products of every shared pair that occur on opposite sides, so the union still satisfies the partial-Steiner uniqueness axiom.
After every identification preserve strongness of the smaller side and decrease the finite strongness budget by at most1; show at most |B minus A| such identifications are needed.
Construct an HF-order with C first on the resulting free amalgam, proving it is unconfined and C remains strong.
For each set X of at most n new C-points, splice the two available HF-orders to prove the embedded B-copy is n-strong.

proof_roadmap.step: A forced product may be moved immediately above the base; adding it consumes at most one unit of n-strongness.
Iteratively identify conflicting products and account for the budget m=n+|B minus A|.
Place C first and then the remaining B-copy, producing an HF-order of the free amalgam.
For any at-most-n set X on the C-side, use the residual strongness and absence of cross blocks to put the B-copy first.

difficulty_reason: Ordinary free union need not even be a partial Steiner system because a common pair can acquire two products. The proof designs a controlled identification process while tracking two distinct strengths of embedding, then constructs compatible HF-orders in both directions. The explicit uniform loss m=n+|B minus A| requires accounting for forced identifications and arbitrary bounded test sets; it is not an invocation of a standard amalgamation theorem.

compared.difference: The public item constructs finite binary trees in an infinite HF-ordered STS. The present claim concerns a quantitative amalgam of finite partial structures and two strengths of embeddings.
The other candidate concerns isomorphism extension in saturated infinite models. Its prepared proof uses tree-based fresh points and closure types, not this n-amalgamation construction.

editorial_notes: C_un is the class of finite unconfined partial Steiner triple systems (source437-440). The whole counted task has finite structures; n-strongness is the bounded test-set condition686-692.
The original author construction and proof are retained. The relation A<=B is strong-substructure order, not the HF linear order itself.

The external support proposition is by the same two authors in Endomorphisms of free Steiner quasigroups, fixed version2412.06055v3. Its finite induction supplies the criterion needed here; the printed infinite compactness clause includes a noted a!=b omission, but the counted finite construction does not use that clause.

In the support source line293, the greatest point of a finite subset A-prime is said to belong to at most one block of A. The needed and directly justified assertion is at most one block inside A-prime: the other two points of each such block lie below that greatest point in the HF-order. The printed broader intermediate wording is retained; the subset restriction follows from the source definition and is the conclusion used here.

source_authorship.known_AI_disclosure: No AI-assistance declaration located in the read source; no assertion about undisclosed author tools.

review_checkpoints: Each identification increases the intersection by one point and removes one point from the outside part of B, so the initial budget n+|B minus A| remains at least n after the process ends.
At termination no common pair has competing products, and blocks involving a point from B minus C and a C-point can only use the shared intersection, since the amalgam has no added cross blocks.
For n-strongness test X subset C minus B, the remaining A-star<=^n C gives an order of A-star union X with A-star first; append X after the B-copy.
No saturated model, monster model, generic existence theorem or compact-expandability theorem is used.

issues_for_independent_review.detail: Judge the simultaneous identification/budget/order-splicing obligations as a whole; do not rate it by its compressed proof length or by the article model-theory title.

For infinite strict-order compactness, totality needs a!=b; the present finite amalgamation uses only the preceding finite induction. The original support proof is retained and the restriction is printed correctly in the main paper780.

The required at-most-one-block conclusion is inside A-prime, as follows directly from its greatest point and the HF definition; the overbroad intermediate wording referring to A remains in the original text and is disclosed.

editorial_scope: One quantitative n-amalgamation proposition for finite unconfined partial Steiner systems. Its identification process and local strongness lemmas are solution obligations. The second source provides the actual HF-ordering criterion. Infinite-model homogeneity, stability, generic existence and the previously published tree lemma are outside this task.
